power_note: Planning, not a criterion: with v1's effect sizes (likely optimistic, as estimates from a near miss tend to be), n = 36 per arm gives about 0.75-0.96 power per strong cell at the strictest Holm step (the 4 MiB cells and 16MiB/8Mbit) and about 0.2 and 0.0 for 16MiB/30Mbit and 16MiB/60Mbit; passing needs 4 of 6, so the chance to pass if the v1 effects are real is roughly one half to two thirds.

slowlive.why: OWN CHOICE of this draft, not derived from real swarms: no stalled peer, but slow and high-latency live peers (2 x 0.25 MB/s at 0.8 +- 0.4 s one-way latency); every ban here is a false ban.

plan.runs: 7 mixed cells (the 6 key cells and the mixed/1MiB/30Mbit guard cell) x 2 arms x 36 = 504 runs; at gsp10-v1's pace for mixed cells (~50 s per run) about 7 h

expected_mechanism.mixed 4/16 MiB: Stalled peers hold blocks of the boundary pieces (16 MiB: piece 0 and the last piece, 4 MiB: mostly the last); CW bans them about 2 s after their first request and their blocks go to live peers at once (G0: 16 MiB edges 11.8 -> 6.3 s, 4 MiB 5.8 -> 4.1 s).
expected_mechanism.mixed 1 MiB: G0: piece 0 unaffected, the last piece delayed (4.4 vs 1.8 s); not a key cell because the 1 MiB start already includes several pieces of buffer.
expected_mechanism.fast / thin / slowlive: No stalled peer: CW must not ban anybody and must not change any time.

risks_not_covered_by_the_probe: A live but high-latency or overloaded peer whose first block takes more than 2 s: it would be banned for 120 s. The slowlive profile covers 0.8 s +- 0.4 s; slower first answers stay untested.
Several real peers behind one NAT address: the IP ban removes all of them for 120 s.

A banned peer gets no upload from us either for 120 s (session-wide ip_filter, every torrent). Negligible on a private tracker where the relay is a short-lived leecher, but a behaviour change; documented as the technical default relay_stall_ban_seconds = 120.
Stalled peers that connect after the serving ones (G0 stall_last without watchdog: 16 MiB piece 0 at 20.8 s): the H1 tracker order is not controlled, so this case is only sampled, not targeted.
Peers that recover after a pause (disk stall) are re-admitted only after the ban; the ban list is capped at 64 addresses (further stalled peers stay connected).
A real outage of our own link does not ban anybody (a peer is banned only while another peer of the same torrent progresses); not exercised by H1.
open_questions: The slowlive profile is this draft's own choice (latency and rate not derived from real swarms).
Real swarms: the frequency of stalled peers is unknown (implementation plan, SP10 row); a PASS shows the synthetic mechanism, not its real-world prevalence.
Whether 120 s is the right ban length is not measured by this gate (only one value is run); it is a technical default.
The harness changes (controller/summarizer/decider hooks) overlap files that the SP03 branch also changed; the merge into the feature branch must keep both opt-in sets.

wiring_smoke.note: Not a measurement: this image, one CW and one C0 run in mixed / 16 MiB / 30 Mbit (draft prerequisites). CW counted 2 bans (the profile has 2 stalled peers), C0 0. The 'duplicate peer-id' check of the draft is not observable here: with capture_log_prefix only the watchdog lines are kept; both runs finished without failure or app traceback.
wiring_smoke.note_v2: From the gsp10-v1 registration: same image and harness.

infra_retry: The controller reruns a run once when it failed by Docker itself (docker run exit 125, 'error waiting for container', 'error during connect', 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon'); the record keeps the first failure as infra_retry. Any other failure stays a failed run.

decision_rule.machine_rule: scripts/decide_sp_gate_bootstrap.py with rule key stall_ban_check (scripts/sp_gate_stall_bans.py); sha256 of both under harness_sha256
decision_rule.primary_metric: start.time_to_start_s (playback start: includes the TTFB, the parallel tail probe of the last piece and the 2 s buffer, i.e. waits for both boundary pieces)
decision_rule.pooling: both series pooled: n = 36 runs per arm and cell; failed runs excluded and counted; v1 data not pooled
decision_rule.statistic: difference of means (CW - C0); 10 000 bootstrap resamples per test, seed 20261111; one-sided bootstrap p-values
decision_rule.improvement: primary metric in a key cell: H0 'difference >= 0' rejected by Holm over the 6 key cells
decision_rule.regression: any guard test (start.time_to_start_s, start.ttfb_s, seek.resume_s, start.stall_s in all 7 cells, 28 tests): H0 'difference <= 0' rejected by Holm over the 28 tests; the mixed/1MiB/30Mbit cell guards the small-piece case flagged descriptively in v1
hard_checks: (b) stalled cells: in every non-failed CW run of a mixed cell app_log.stall_bans <= 2 (the profile's stalled peers)
(c) wiring: app_log.stall_bans == 0 in every non-failed C0 run (switch off)
a missing counter in any non-failed C0 or CW run fails the check
failed runs and tracebacks with an application frame: CW <= C0

(a) false bans in swarms without stalled peers: not re-run; gsp10-v1 on the same image and harness found 0 bans in all 60 CW runs of the fast, thin and slowlive cells (carried evidence, gsp10-v1-assessment.json)
pass_if_all: at least 4 of 6 key cells improved
failed runs and application tracebacks: CW <= C0
reported_not_required: CW runs with at least one ban in the mixed cells (attribution of an improvement to the watchdog)
decision_rule.count_limit: Counts cannot tell a stalled peer's ban from a serving peer's ban inside a mixed cell: (b) bounds that case, (a) is the false-ban check. A seed-side check (was a serving seeder disconnected by a ban) would need a change to the seed fixture whose hash earlier protocols pin; not done.
decision_rule.v2_changes: Only the run count (10 -> 36 per arm and cell, as two series of 18), the cell set (the 7 mixed cells; the fast/thin/slowlive cells, which v1 covered without regression or false ban on the same image, are not re-run) and the bootstrap seed. Primary metric, key cells, improved_required 4 of 6, alpha, Holm families, hard checks (b) and (c), traceback and failed-run rules are v1's.
